All six namespace_term reads (rdf:type, solid:TypeRegistration, solid:forClass, skos:Concept, wiki:Source, schema:Person) become prefixed names, resolved at transpile time to constant URIRefs -- confirmed with `ldpy -t` (transpile-only): each one is inlined as `_ldpy_.URIRef('...')`, correctly scoped (the function-local prefixes do not leak, the module-level ones are visible inside the function per declarations.md block scope). No DefinedNamespace subclass is involved here, so none of the sibling regions' not-expressible pattern applies -- this translation is directly-expressible on its own terms.

The fixture=/entry= reading-oracle protocol (corpus/405) does not fit this region regardless of the above: run_pair calls `entry(fixture_graph(...))`, passing the parsed graph as the function's SOLE argument, but test_type_index_has_wiki_registrations takes NO parameters -- it acquires and parses its own graph internally via the network call. Restructuring it to accept a graph parameter would remove the network fetch, which is precisely the behaviour under test (per instructions, no refactoring); fixture.ttl is written to the shape the instructions require (several solutions, a zero-solution case, non-matching neighbourhood) for documentation, but is not actually wired through run_pair's fixture= mechanism for this reason.
